newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura bids for six pct of bonds in 10-yr JGB sale.
newsitem.headline: Nomura bids for six pct of bonds in 10-yr JGB sale.

text.p: Nomura Securities Co Ltd took about six percent of the bonds at Tuesday's Japanese government bond (JGB) auction, bond traders said.
There had been speculation that Nomura might try to get a larger share before an expected order to refrain from the bond business due to improper payments by two of its directors.
Traders said Japan's biggest brokerage bid about 35 billion yen in the auction.
A senior dealer at Nomura did not confirm the volume, but said, "We bid the bond for our trading inventory."
The Minstry of Finance offers 10-year JGBs every month. The newly auctioned bond, carrying a record low coupon rate of 2.5 percent, is issued in April.
MOF said all accepted bids totalled 591.14 billion yen as about 60 percent of the offered volume of one trillion yen was covered by the auction.

Regulators are currently investigating Nomura over its March 6 admission that two of its managing directors made discretionary transactions banned under Japanese law and funnelled profits to a corporate client linked to a racketeer.
Bond traders expect that MOF will take similar steps to its 1991 action banning Nomura from bond underwriting and auction participation in JGBs and government-guaranteed bonds for two months.
In 1991 Nomura was found to have violated the Securities and Exchange Law through an excessive sales campaign for shares in railway firm Tokyu Corp.
